bullets.text: YOY growth rate down significantly from prior three years, reflecting soft market conditions expected to continue; new business on pace with last year, stronger in Direct than Agency.

Announced 'Drive Insurance from Progressive' for independent agents and brokers, formally launching December 10th; provides clarity between consumer offerings. More than 80% of U.S. auto insurance is written through captive and independent agents.
Dutch auction tender offer purchased 16.9M common shares at $88/share, reducing outstanding shares by approximately 7.8% from 217.0M at the end of the third quarter.
Hurricane claims response closed 94% of reported damage claims, approaching 80% closed within 20 to 25 days post-incident; after-action review planned to identify further service improvements.

Renewal business provided an increased percentage of premium and growth, and efforts focus on increasing customer retention. Retention measures were expected to increase with rate stability, but observed measures fell during the quarter.

Based on YTD written premiums through Q2, the industry auto insurance segment grew an estimated 4%. Among top 15 private passenger auto insurers, Progressive Direct grew fastest at 17%, with Agency sixth at 11%.

Created separate brand identities for Agency and Direct; independent agents sought greater participation and recognition in advertising, which was difficult under a single brand primarily promoting Direct attributes.
After a period of increase, average premium per policy is essentially flat year-to-date. Market conditions and competitor actions suggest no immediate outlook for premium increases.
Received subpoenas regarding industrywide broker bid-rigging and antitrust investigations; no regulator has suggested Progressive is an investigation target, nor does management believe it should be.
Achieved performance standards required for concierge claims strategy expansion; plans to announce multiple new locations shortly for site development and scheduled openings in 2005.
